**4B.1 Research Note**

Assessment: **mostly negative**. Erdoğan’s 2024 record shows real electoral competition existed, but the broader political environment remained heavily tilted by media control, bans on critics, and punitive treatment of opposition officeholders. I did not find strong evidence that he genuinely embraced free, fair, and meaningful alternation of power as a governing principle.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Weak positive | [Erdoğan suffered major local-election defeat](https://apnews.com/article/8adc4df56cdbce24f78900e1d142ff21) | Associated Press | 2024-03-31 | https://apnews.com/article/8adc4df56cdbce24f78900e1d142ff21 | Erdoğan’s party lost Istanbul and Ankara and the nationwide popular vote in the March local elections, showing that incumbency could be defeated electorally in 2024. This is evidence of contestability, though not of Erdoğan’s sincere acceptance of it. | 4B.1; 3B.8 |
| Negative | [Digital News Report 2024: Turkey](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The report describes continued tight media control and says the local-election campaign remained structurally favorable to incumbency. That undercuts the idea of fully free and meaningful electoral contestation. | 4B.1; 3B.8; 3B.6 |
| Negative | [Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says the regime routinely restricted gatherings critical of the government, used force against protests, and preserved a tilted political environment. That is inconsistent with genuine acceptance of open, fair competition. | 4B.1; 3B.8; 3B.5 |
| Negative | [Turkey government removes elected opposition mayors](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-11-06 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors | After the elections, the government removed elected mayors, detained a mayor on terrorism charges, dissolved councils, and police dispersed protests. This shows that electoral outcomes were not fully respected when they threatened ruling-party control. | 4B.1; 3B.8; 3B.2; 3B.1 |
| Negative | [Türkiye: Kurdish politicians convicted in unjust mass trial](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/16/turkiye-kurdish-politicians-convicted-unjust-mass-trial) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-16 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/16/turkiye-kurdish-politicians-convicted-unjust-mass-trial | HRW says 24 Kurdish politicians were convicted on bogus charges in a manifestly political trial. That points to a system that punishes meaningful opposition rather than genuinely competing with it. | 4B.1; 3B.2; 3B.8 |

**Search gap**

I found evidence that elections still produced real opposition victories, but I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Erdoğan personally or institutionally embraced a norm of free, fair, and meaningful contestability. The strongest evidence instead points to a managed, uneven playing field and post-election coercion against opposition figures.
